A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Gated DeltaNet work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison. Local text overlap on v2 page 5 is recoverable through text extraction.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training and evaluations, retrieval and length-extrapolation results, throughput measurements, and component and hybrid ablations in Tables S.1–S.2.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark comparisons, throughput measurements and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: The defining gated recurrence (v1 Eq. 8; v2 Eq. 10), token-mixer components and H1/H2 hybrid architectures are retained. The revised derivation does not establish a redesigned method; its non-equivalent printed expressions are assessed under T1.

E1.justification: FineWeb-Edu training, commonsense evaluation, S-NIAH, real-world retrieval, length extrapolation and LongBench coverage remain unchanged. S-NIAH-3 is relabeled from word to UUID retrieval in the main text, but retains identical results and the same appendix description; no new evaluated scenario is established.

E2.justification: All benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. However, v1 Section 3.1 footnote 1 reports an empirical comparison between Longhorn-style implicit and DeltaNet-style explicit updates; v2 footnote 3 retains only their theoretical distinction, removing that limited empirical comparison.

E3.justification: The reported training and evaluation settings remain unchanged, including 1.3B models trained on 100B tokens, 4K training sequences, 2K sliding windows and retrieval truncation, and the appendix ablation budgets. v2's explicit zero-shot S-NIAH caption adds documentation without establishing a protocol change.

E4.justification: The component, normalization, head-dimension and hybrid-order ablations remain identical, as do the length-extrapolation analyses. The S-NIAH case study reuses existing evidence. The limited removal is v1's qualitative check of whether implicit versus explicit update formulations differ empirically.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or identifiable significance-testing procedures. v1's removed informal statement about no significant performance difference does not specify a statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Numerical results match across the renumbered language-modeling and S-NIAH tables, Tables 4–5, Tables S.1–S.2 and Figures 2–3. The change is removal of v1's unquantified finding of no significant empirical performance difference between the Longhorn-style and DeltaNet-style update approaches.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the UT inverse from I minus lower(...) to I plus strictLower(...) and corrects the local decay-ratio orientation. However, its Section 3.3 output equation replaces v1 Eq. 12's decay mask Gamma with plain causal mask M, without equivalent compensating factors, creating an inconsistency with the retained recurrence. The appendix induction proof is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: combining gating with delta updates, enabling efficient parallel training, outperforming existing recurrent models, and improving performance and throughput through hybrid architectures.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly interprets UUID retrieval as testing complex-pattern memorization and separates retention, filtering and memorization mechanisms. It also qualifies the structured-transition reasoning claim from substantially improving capabilities to potentially enabling them, and expands discussion of expressiveness versus parallelism for alternative online-learning formulations.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies S-NIAH evaluation as zero-shot with 1.3B models and adds FLA implementation links. It removes v1's chunk-size guidance—multiples of 16, typically 64—and forward-substitution explanation. Core hyperparameters, hardware disclosure and the main project link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Research positioning expands substantially through discussion of concurrent RWKV-7 and Titans, DeltaProduct, test-time regression, Mesa-style learning, nonlinear-recurrence parallelization and additional hybrid architectures. v2 also replaces the earlier Longhorn/TTT critique and adds a dedicated hybrid-model discussion, changing the substantive relationship to surrounding research.

P1.justification: v2 extensively reorganizes the preliminaries and chunkwise derivation, moves and rewrites S-NIAH evaluation as Section 3.2, revises much of related work, and moves ablations from Appendix A.2 to B.2. These are substantial narrative and structural changes despite stable benchmark evidence.

P2.justification: The same figures and tables are retained, with relocation, renumbering, caption changes and some resizing. The S-NIAH table moves earlier and gains a revised caption and UUID label. v2 page 5 introduces visible overlap between the table and prose, and between an introductory sentence and a case-study heading.

improvement.justification: v2 broadens research context, clarifies the memory-mechanism discussion and corrects UT signs. These benefits coexist with a newly inconsistent chunkwise output equation and visible page 5 overlaps. Since the benchmark evidence remains unchanged and the mathematical revision both corrects and introduces errors, a reliable net quality direction is unclear.
